clue.text: Room in hospital needs right decoration and furniture

parts.note: a hospital room for patients is a ward
the OBE (Order of the British Empire) is a British honour or decoration

explanation.surface: A hospital room needs proper decor and furnishing.
explanation.definitionFit: A wardrobe is a tall cupboard for hanging clothes, a piece of bedroom furniture.

clue.text: They are loopy — requesting, identification of an author, by his initials

parts.note: asking 'who?' requests someone's identity
RLS are the initials of Robert Louis Stevenson

explanation.surface: Mad people ask an author to sign with his initials.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'Who? RLS': a question and the initials of Robert Louis Stevenson, author of Treasure Island.
explanation.definitionFit: Whorls are spirals or coils, as on fingertips, so they form loops.

clue.text: Green colouring of the Red Sea

indicators.note: colouring the words disguises them, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The green hue of the Red Sea, a contradiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'colouring' disguises REDSEA as the same six letters in another order.
explanation.definitionFit: Reseda, named after the mignonette plant, is a greyish-green shade.

clue.text: Take river fish on a reel perhaps — it's good to dispose of it

definitions.text: it's good to dispose of it

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river
the id or ide is a freshwater fish
a reel is a Scottish dance

explanation.surface: Catching a river fish on a fishing reel, which you are then glad to get rid of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reel' is not fishing tackle but a lively Scottish dance; the definition plays on 'good riddance'.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting rid of something unwanted is its riddance, hence 'good riddance'.

clue.text: Dress up for a game

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: garb is clothing or dress

explanation.surface: Putting on fancy clothes for a party game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns GARB around, as befits a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Brag is a three-card gambling game, an ancestor of poker.

clue.text: Spring vegetable?

definitions.meaning: to spring up is to shoot or emerge, as a seedling does
a Brussels ... is a small green vegetable

explanation.definitionFit: To shoot up from the ground is to burgeon; the Brussels variety is a leafy green eaten at Christmas.

clue.text: Top dressing for eccentric peer, in Britain

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other
eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters of peer are rearranged

parts.note: UK is the United Kingdom, Britain

explanation.surface: A distinctive hat for an odd nobleman in Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' gives PERE from PEER, and UK goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A peruke is a long periwig, which is worn on the head.

clue.text: hop and writhe in this fashion

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'hop and writhe in this fashion' starts lower case and looks cut short: HOPAND lacks the two I's that OPHIDIAN needs, and no search found the full clue.
annotationWithheld.clue: hop and writhe in this fashion

clue.text: Formerly, red wine then whiskies and soda-that's what the guys were attached to

definitions.text: what the guys were attached to

parts.note: tent is an old name for a dark red Spanish wine
a peg is an Anglo-Indian word for a whisky and soda

explanation.surface: Old-time drinking: red wine, then whisky-sodas, which the men clung to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guys' are not men but the ropes that hold a tent up.
explanation.definitionFit: Guy ropes are fastened to the stakes driven into the ground round a tent.

clue.text: Stone egg — and ibis is confused

parts.note: an egg is shaped like the letter O

indicators.note: being confused, these letters are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: An egg and an ibis are somehow mixed up together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egg' is the shape of a letter here, and 'confused' is the anagram signal; 'is' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Obsidian is a glassy black volcanic rock.

clue.text: Mischievous youngster can be prickly

definitions.meaning: a scruffy, impish child
the sea creature and the old name for a hedgehog are both spiny

explanation.definitionFit: A street brat shares the name with spiny animals like the sea echinoid and, archaically, the hedgehog.

clue.text: Quarters for troops in which there are bars

definitions.meaning: lodgings where soldiers are housed
small bars of metal, or rectangles in heraldry

explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers' lodgings in private homes are billets, and the word also means short bars of wood, metal or heraldic oblongs.

clue.text: Luxuriously sensuous-sounding girl heading north

parts.note: Lydia is a girl's name
a compass heading of north is abbreviated N

explanation.surface: A girl with a voluptuous voice sets off northwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lydian mode of ancient Greek music was thought soft and voluptuous, so the word describes indulgent, sensuous music.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient Lydia was famed for luxury, so its music and manners were proverbially soft and voluptuous.

clue.text: Improved when collected

definitions.meaning: trade or health that got better
fetched, gathered or lifted

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both recovered or got better and fetched someone from a place.

clue.text: It's not a roundabout, where the lines run out

definitions.text: It's not a roundabout, where the lines run out

parts.words: It's not a roundabout, where the lines run out
parts.note: a stopping place for trains, not a traffic circle, from which railway tracks run out in different directions

explanation.surface: A traffic junction where the road markings end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roundabout' and 'lines' suggest roads; the lines are railway tracks, and the place stays put rather than going round.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway terminus is where tracks begin and trains halt.

clue.text: Sink beside the fire

definitions.meaning: to sink a ship deliberately
the coal bucket kept next to the hearth

explanation.definitionFit: To scuttle a vessel is to hole it so it goes down; a coal scuttle is the hearthside container.

clue.text: A smack of seaweed

definitions.meaning: a smack is a taste or flavour, as in 'a smack of garlic'
a name for large coarse seaweeds such as wrack

explanation.definitionFit: A sharp flavour is a tang, and the word also names kelp-like wrack on the shore.

clue.text: Official gets a little information on the personnel

parts.note: a tip is a small piece of useful advice
staff are the people employed

explanation.surface: A manager receives a hint about the workforce.
explanation.walkthrough: A TIPSTAFF is a court officer, named after the metal-tipped staff he carried.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipstaff is a sheriff's officer or court usher.

clue.text: Change-it's all on a horse

indicators.note: change means the order of these letters is altered

parts.note: the apostrophe drops and the S stays

explanation.surface: A punter backs a horse, staking everything on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A stallion is an uncastrated male horse.

clue.text: Fix sails in angry water

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: irate means angry
to rig a ship is to fit its sails

explanation.walkthrough: 'water' is not the sea but a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To irrigate land is to supply it with water.

clue.text: I love to get thanks in a letter, abroad

parts.note: love is a score of nil in tennis, written O
ta is informal British for thanks

explanation.surface: Someone is delighted to receive a written thank-you while overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' says the letter belongs to a foreign alphabet: here the Greek one.
explanation.definitionFit: Iota is the ninth character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Those who utter coins you can't spend

definitions.meaning: people who state or declare things
ancient Greek coins, long out of circulation

explanation.definitionFit: People who declare things are its literal sense; it is also the name of gold or silver coins of ancient Greece.

clue.text: Flyers set off outside — to do so?

indicators.note: outside says the jumbled letters wrap round the other piece
off means the word set is out of order, its letters jumbled

parts.note: the RAF, the Royal Air Force, is made up of flyers

explanation.surface: Airmen set off on a mission: is that what they do?
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' turns SET into STE, placed 'outside' RAF. The definition refers back to the flyers: attacking from low-flying aircraft is what they would do.
explanation.definitionFit: To strafe is to attack ground targets with machine-gun fire from low-flying aircraft.

clue.text: Swallow most of the drink

indicators.note: most of says the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: a martini is a cocktail

explanation.surface: Gulp down almost all the cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallow' is not a verb but the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The house martin is a bird of the swallow family.

clue.text: Make good and go

definitions.meaning: to fix something broken
to ... to a place is to go there

explanation.definitionFit: To mend is one sense, and to betake oneself somewhere, as in 'repair to the bar', is the other.

clue.text: For this, a liquid mixture is the answer

definitions.meaning: a substance dissolved in a liquid
the answer to a problem or puzzle

explanation.definitionFit: Chemists call something dissolved in a solvent this, and a puzzle's resolved answer is the same word.

clue.text: Six simple to face

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
a simple is an old word for a medicinal herb, such as sage

explanation.walkthrough: 'simple' is not 'easy' but the noun: an old name for a medicinal plant, here the herb SAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A visage is a person's countenance.

clue.text: Laughter in the depression

definitions.meaning: the sound of laughing
a sunken ditch serving as a hidden boundary in a garden or park

explanation.definitionFit: The written laugh is also a sunk fence, a ditch that bounds a landscaped park without blocking the view.

clue.text: Article on weird Mali creature

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: weird signals that the letters of the word Mali come out in an odd order

explanation.surface: A news article about strange goings-on in Mali.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weird' is the anagram signal working on the country name; 'on' just joins the article to it.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal is any living beast.

clue.text: A man's hat adapted to fit her

indicators.note: adapted means altered to fit, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: the possessive here keeps its S as a letter

explanation.surface: A man's hat is altered so that a woman can wear it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adapted' rearranges AMANSHAT; 'her' is the definition, a woman of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: Samantha is a woman's first name, so a female person, 'her'.

clue.text: Answered evasively and so created a barrier

definitions.meaning: parried questions, dodged them
put up a fence around something

explanation.definitionFit: To parry questions is the figurative sense, like a swordsman; putting up a railing or paling is the literal one.

clue.text: Providing local produce, as it were

definitions.text: Providing local produce, as it were

parts.words: Providing local produce, as it were
parts.note: in Britain the local is the neighbourhood pub, so its produce is beer, and the person providing it keeps an inn

explanation.walkthrough: 'local' looks like farm produce from nearby, but in Britain 'the local' is one's neighbourhood pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A taverner is an innkeeper, who serves drink at the local pub.
